AC-A1 requires blocking on 'anything other than a clean VISUAL_VERIFIED result' in auto mode, so the fix-round-succeeds-but-redegrades sub-case should route to VISUAL_GATE_BLOCKED, but Task 5's literal 'Otherwise' enumeration does not name it, leaving whether this specific sub-case is gated ambiguous rather than structurally guaranteed.

R8a and R8c pass (source PRD APPROVED; Implementation Phases row 5 Status=in-progress with matching PRP Plan cell). R8b's attempt-1 format defect is fixed — AC-A5 now carries a well-formed (PRD AC-N) token — but the substantive citation is still wrong: AC-A5 was retagged to (PRD AC-6), and AC-6's actual claim (phase_scope:logic Phase A.3.4 non-blocking outcome-recording, i.e. command-routing-layer regression preservation) is already precisely and completely claimed by this same plan's AC-A2 (near-verbatim restatement of AC-6); AC-6 never mentions interaction scripts, capture.mjs, or per-frame behavior. AC-A5's actual claim (capture.mjs performs zero interaction-related Playwright calls when a frame's interaction is absent/none) is the structural, same-mechanism sibling of AC-A4 (the 'interaction present' case, sharing the identical Tasks 1/2/3 ADDRESSES lists), which is already tied to PRD AC-4. The internally consistent, substantively grounded fix is to retag AC-A5 as (PRD AC-4) to match AC-A4, or fold AC-A5 into AC-A4 — not (PRD AC-6). The 'byte-identical'/'identical to today's v1 behavior' vocabulary overlap between AC-A5 and AC-6 is surface word-echo, not a genuine claim correspondence: both AC-4 and AC-6 describe the Phase A.3.4 outer gate's blocking/non-blocking routing; AC-A5 describes the inner script's (capture.mjs) per-frame behavior — closer in subject matter to AC-4/AC-A4's interaction-execution-correctness claim than to AC-6's phase-scope routing claim.

Progress from attempt 1: the specific missing sub-case (fix-round-succeeds sub-case re-dispatching to VISUAL_DEGRADED) is now explicitly named and closed by construction via the auto-mode bullet's allow-list form ('proceed ONLY when... VISUAL_VERIFIED... For every OTHER point... do NOT proceed') — this correctly closes the attempt-1 gap, and no stray branch-count word survives the paragraph. However, full re-verification surfaces a new, more fundamental robustness concern: Task 5's ACTION explicitly declares Step B's own bullets 'untouched by this task', and Step B's own text (plugins/relay/commands/relay-implement.md:388-395, unedited) still says unconditionally '...proceed to Phase A.3.5' inside every branch, including the fix-round-succeeds sub-case ('Otherwise (...): set visual_outcome from that re-dispatch's own verdict ("APPROVED" or the named degraded rung); proceed to Phase A.3.5.', line 394) and the plain VISUAL_VERIFIED bullet. Task 5 inserts the new gating paragraph as an UNNUMBERED paragraph after Step B (item 5) and before No commit issued (item 6), relying on the executing agent inferring that this later paragraph overrides Step B's own literal, unedited 'proceed to Phase A.3.5' claims for the human-mode and auto-mode-non-VISUAL_VERIFIED cases. This differs from the file's one nearby precedent for 'later content after Step B still applies' (item 6, purely ADDITIVE, never contradicting Step B) — the new paragraph, by contrast, directly CONTRADICTS Step B's own text for at least one condition (human mode + a genuine VISUAL_VERIFIED result: Step B says proceed, the new paragraph says do NOT proceed). The plan's prose correctly signals the intended override, but AC-A1's blocking guarantee should be closed by construction (editing the contradicting text itself) rather than by relying on inference to resolve a textual contradiction between an unnumbered later paragraph and unedited numbered list items. Recommended fix: have Task 5 (or a companion edit) also touch Step B's own bullets — e.g. replace each 'proceed to Phase A.3.5' occurrence inside Step B with a forward-reference to the Terminal routing paragraph below, or fold the gating logic directly into Step B's own bullets.

Task 5's closing sentence ('## Step-by-Step Tasks') reads: 'max_visual_retries=2 is the SAME budget variable step 4 (Step A/Budget init) already initializes.' This contradicts Task 4's own renumbering instruction in the same plan section: Task 4 renumbers existing items 3/4/5 (Step A/Step B/No commit issued) to 4/5/6 and inserts a NEW item 3 'between the existing item 2 (Budget init.) and the newly-renumbered item 4 (Step A)' — i.e. post-Task-4, Budget init remains item 2 (never renumbered) and Step A becomes item 4; these are two different steps, not one joint 'step 4 (Step A/Budget init)'. max_visual_retries is actually initialized in step 2 (Budget init), not step 4 (Step A). Minor and non-blocking on its own, but a factual cross-reference error the Implementer would carry into the shipped relay-implement.md if left uncorrected.

Task 2's ACTION (## Step-by-Step Tasks) inserts the function definition `async function executeInteractionSteps(page, steps) { ... }` immediately after parseInteractionScript() and BEFORE captureFrame() - structurally before the page.goto call inside captureFrame - then separately inserts the call site `await executeInteractionSteps(page, interactionSteps);` inside captureFrame, between the existing page.goto and page.screenshot lines. Task 2's VALIDATE (third node -e block) computes `const execIdx = src.indexOf('executeInteractionSteps(page');` and requires `execIdx > gotoIdx` to pass. The literal substring `executeInteractionSteps(page` occurs in BOTH the function definition and the call site; `indexOf` returns the FIRST (leftmost) match, which is the definition (placed before captureFrame per the ACTION, hence before gotoIdx) - not the call site. So `execIdx > gotoIdx` evaluates false unconditionally, and this VALIDATE sub-check FAILS on every correctly-implemented attempt regardless of code correctness - the same ACTION-to-VALIDATE impossibility class this round's context specifically asked to guard against (re: Task 5's marker count). Illustrative fix: use `src.lastIndexOf(...)` for execIdx (the call site is the later of the two occurrences), or search a call-site-unique substring such as `await executeInteractionSteps(page` (the definition is never preceded by `await `).
